narratives.Overview:
1. Buffer (P1). `gitFenceSpawn` (`packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts`) passes `maxBuffer: SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER`. The readers that return file content through it (the merge-base brief read, the policy read and the mint head-brief read) keep their `error` and `signal` checks ahead of the status check, so an overflow past 64 MiB is still detected and never parsed as text. The `rev-parse`, `merge-base` and delivery-branch lookups through it return refs and SHAs and are unchanged apart from the option.
2. Reason on a failed policy read (P2). `readMergeBasePolicyRaw` returns `{ kind: "error", detail }`. The detail is the first of: the spawn error message, `git show killed by signal <S>`, git's trimmed stderr, or `git show exited <N>`. It never uses stdout. The detail has newlines removed, is cut to at most 300 characters, and is wrapped with `fenceUntrustedAcceptanceText`.
3. Fail-closed shape (P2). In `loadOnePrMintFence`, `basePolicy.kind === "error"` returns `unreadableFence("merge-base:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json", detail)`, the result a failed brief read already returns, instead of `emptyFence()`. A policy blob absent from the merge base, and a policy that reads as level off, keep today's empty fence. The error result stays unmemoized, as today.
4. Deny text (P2). `formatPositiveGoverningAllowDeny` (`packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts`) gets one branch ahead of the others: when the fence is unreadable, it returns "Directive denied this mutation: the selected running scope's write fence could not be read (<unreadableDetail>), so its one-PR mint was not checked (#6602). Recovery: retry; if it repeats, report it, and land the brief through a separate activation PR so it is on the merge base." The deny code and the other callers' existing unreadable messages (`dispatcher.ts` 1649-1657 and 5702-5710) are unchanged.
5. Unpinned contest (P2). When `inspectActiveScope` returns the unpinned `multiple-eligible` result (`scope.ts` 526-532) and a brief in that competition set has an unreadable fence, the result carries the first such fence's `unreadableDetail` in a new optional field, and its message adds one sentence naming that brief and the detail. The fences are the ones the partition already loads; no extra read. In the dispatcher's #6535 site (b) (`dispatcher.ts` 3098-3115), `warnableScopeMiss` is false when that field is set, so the existing `scope-not-ready` deny is returned. Pinned and bound selections, other `multiple-eligible` results, `zero-eligible` and `pin-miss` are unchanged, and a not-ready scope whose briefs were all read keeps its #6535 warning.
6. Other hook reads (P3). `readStagedBlob` (`packages/core/src/hooks/planning-publication.ts`) passes `maxBuffer: SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER`. No other capture changes: on the agent-hook write decision and in the verbs the deposited `.githooks/pre-commit` and `.githooks/pre-push` run, the other git captures return names, refs or SHAs, already pass a ceiling (`defaultGitRunner`, the small-change runner, the 16 MiB pre-push blob hash), or read files from disk.
7. Unchanged: `createScopeProvenanceGit`, `defaultGitRunner`, the #5656 positive-allow requirement, the one-PR evaluators, and `PROJECT-DEFINITION` itself. The #6535 warner keeps its rules apart from item 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a merge base whose `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` is larger than 1 MiB (for example 2 MiB) with `onePrScopeProof` at `mint`, and a brief absent from the merge base with a matching same-PR mint record, when `loadStoryWriteFenceFromMergeBase` runs, then it returns that brief's `file_scope` with `onePrMint.admitted` true, and a Write inside that scope is allowed.
- Given the same large policy with the level off, or a merge base without the policy blob, then the fence is empty as today.
- Given the policy read fails (spawn error, signal, or a non-zero exit that is not a missing path) for the one selected brief, then the fence is unreadable, its detail names `merge-base:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`, and a Write is refused with the item 4 text.
- Given the same failure while the #6535 merge-gate signal is live, then the Write is still refused (the runtime-policy unreadable deny is not warnable), and the prospective scope cover refuses with its existing unreadable message.
- Given two unpinned eligible briefs, one with a failed policy read and one with a readable `file_scope`, with or without a live merge-gate signal, then the Write is refused with `scope-not-ready`, and the message names the unreadable brief and the read failure.
- Given two unpinned eligible briefs whose fences were both read, under a live merge-gate signal, then the #6535 warning applies as today.
- Given git prints 10 KB of stderr, or stdout holds part of the blob, then the reason in the deny has at most 300 characters of detail, is fenced, and contains no stdout bytes.
- Given a staged `plan-sequence.json` blob larger than 1 MiB, then `readStagedBlob` returns its text.
narratives.Constraint:
- Keeping `emptyFence()` for a failed policy read with only a note on the deny (comment 6966654494, finding 1): it lets a write through under the merge-gate warning and changes the unpinned contest.
- Letting the #6535 site (b) warning continue a not-ready contest that holds an unreadable fence (comment 6966857234, finding 1): the write would run with no story fence at all.
- Treating a failed policy read as non-fencing in the contest: that is the empty-fence behaviour finding 1 of comment 6966654494 refused.
- Routing the fence through `createScopeProvenanceGit` (adds a throwing timeout to every fence spawn) or `defaultGitRunner` (drops `error` and `signal`) (comment 6966654494, finding 2).
- Treating status 0 as success when `error` is set (comment 6966654494, finding 2): truncated bytes would parse as level off.
- Putting stdout, or uncapped stderr, into the deny (comment 6966654494, finding 3).
- Slimming `PROJECT-DEFINITION` below 1 MiB as the fix (#3156).
- A larger special ceiling for this one read: 64 MiB is the shared ceiling, and a read past it gets the unreadable refusal.

## In plain English
The hook write fence reads the merge-base copy of `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` with `git show` through Node's `spawnSync`, with no buffer size. Node's default is 1 MiB. The file is now 1,092,575 bytes, so the read stops with ENOBUFS. The fence then treats the policy as unknown, does not check the one-PR mint, and refuses every write for a story whose brief is not yet on the merge base, with the generic "no file_scope" message. CI admits the same brief, because its git reader has a 64 MiB buffer. The recommended fix gives the fence's git helper the same 64 MiB buffer, keeps the refusal when the policy still cannot be read but names the reason in the deny, and checks the other git reads on the hook write path for the same default.

## Pains
#6602 has no Acceptance Criteria heading. These three pains are derived from its Summary and Fix sections.
- P1 — Once the merge-base `PROJECT-DEFINITION` passes 1 MiB, every one-PR story (#6273 / #6361) is refused on every Write and Edit, although `verify:scope-provenance` in CI admits the same brief.
- P2 — When the merge-base policy cannot be read, the deny shows the generic #5656 no-file_scope text, so the operator cannot see that the policy read failed or what to do.
- P3 — Other git reads on the agent-hook write path that return whole file content may use the same 1 MiB default and fail the same way as their files grow.

## Constraints (not pains)
- Add no gate and no grant. Prefer the smallest rule. A fix removes a failure mode; it does not add a check.
- Not a fix: slimming `PROJECT-DEFINITION` under 1 MiB to make the read pass (#3156). Its growth is not a pain of this arc.
- When the policy truly cannot be read, the write stays refused: the mint is never treated as admitted without a check.
- Running stories not to overlap: #6480 (`hooks/scope.ts`, `hooks/dispatcher.ts`, `scope/lands-with-product.ts`, `policy/write-fence.ts`). The build must sequence after it or check `parallel_safe`.

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA
- `packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts` 247-268 `gitFenceSpawn`: `spawnSync("git", …, { cwd, encoding: "utf8", stdio })`, no `maxBuffer`. Every fence git call goes through it: `rev-parse` (386, 449), `merge-base` (469), the merge-base brief `git show` (519), the policy `git show` (544-549) and the mint head-brief `git show` (655).
- `write-fence.ts` 544-553 `readMergeBasePolicyRaw`: `error` or `signal` → `{ kind: "error" }` with no detail. 767-776: the brief is absent from the merge base, so the policy is read; an `error` result is not memoized. 672-680 `loadOnePrMintFence`: `basePolicy.kind === "error"` → `emptyFence()`.
- Reproduced at the dispatch SHA with Node 24: `spawnSync("git", ["show", "<sha>:xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json"], { encoding: "utf8" })` returns status 0, `error.code` ENOBUFS, 1,064,597 characters of stdout.
- `packages/core/src/subprocess/max-buffer.ts` 1-17: `SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER` = 64 MiB, with the rule that large captures must pass it. Users include `session/git.ts` 46-51 (`defaultGitRunner`) and `scope-provenance/git-call.ts` 207 (CI reader).
- `packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` 61-90: `POSITIVE_GOVERNING_ALLOW_REQUIRED` and `formatPositiveGoverningAllowDeny` (mint reason only when `onePrMint.admitted` is false).
- Fence consumers: `hooks/dispatcher.ts` 3134-3146 (positive allow; #6535 warner on writes), 1632-1663 (runtime-policy direct write; unreadable → deny), 5700-5722 (prospective scope cover: unreadable → deny without `advisoryCapable`; empty → deny with `advisoryCapable: true`); `hooks/scope.ts` 276-299 (unpinned partition: unreadable counts as fencing, empty does not).
- Other git captures near the hook write path: `hooks/planning-publication.ts` 124-134 `readStagedBlob` (`git cat-file blob`, no `maxBuffer`; reads the staged `plan-sequence.json`); `hooks/dispatcher.ts` 5348-5361 and `hooks/scope.ts` 1276-1287 (names and refs only); `policy/branch-sync.ts` 215-218 (`git show` of the policy through `defaultGitRunner`, already bounded); `write-fence.ts` 583-642 `newestInRangeCommitWithPath` (through `defaultGitRunner`).

## Recommended mechanism (the thing to critique)
- M1 (P1). `gitFenceSpawn` passes `maxBuffer: SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER`. One option, so every fence read shares the CI cap. No new shared reader: `defaultGitRunner` trims stdout and drops `error` and `signal`, which the fence needs.
- M2 (P2). `readMergeBasePolicyRaw` keeps a detail on its `error` result (the spawn error message, the signal, or git's stderr). `loadOnePrMintFence` still returns an empty fence for that case, so the write is still refused, with the same deny code, the same `advisoryCapable` and the same partition result as today. It adds one optional note on the fence view that only `formatPositiveGoverningAllowDeny` reads: the deny then says that the merge-base `PROJECT-DEFINITION` could not be read (the detail, fenced as untrusted text), that the one-PR mint was not checked, and that the brief can land through a separate activation PR meanwhile. The error branch does not become an unreadable fence, because that would add refusals (runtime-policy deny, no advisory on scope cover, a change in partition).
- M3 (P3). On the agent-hook write path, a git call that returns whole file content passes `SUBPROCESS_MAX_BUFFER`: the fence reads in M1 and `readStagedBlob`. The other captures on that path return names, refs or SHAs, or already use `defaultGitRunner`, and stay as they are.
- M4. A test reads a merge-base `PROJECT-DEFINITION` larger than 1 MiB and gets the one-PR mint result that CI gets.

Questions for the critic:
1. Is a per-call `maxBuffer` in `gitFenceSpawn` enough, or is a shared reader with CI (`createScopeProvenanceGit`) needed for parity?
2. Is "empty fence plus a deny note" the right fail-closed shape for an unreadable policy, or does any consumer let a write through on an empty fence that an unreadable policy should refuse?
3. Is there any other git read on the agent-hook write path (or in the deposited git hooks) that returns file content without a bound?

Code was read from the dest checkout. The shell hook refused `git show` because `node_modules/@deftai/directive-runtime` is missing. The worktree HEAD file is `e506478e9305a8006c3545b5e161fcb0982a0d87`.

## In plain English

The agent write hook loads the merge-base copy of `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json` through `git show`. That capture uses Node's 1 MiB default. The file is larger, the capture fails, and the one-PR path then behaves as if the story had an empty allow-list. The write is refused with the generic no-allow-list text. The CI check reads the same blob with a 64 MiB limit and can admit the story.

The buffer half of the recommended mechanism holds. One 64 MiB limit on the fence's own git helper removes this refusal for a file that fits. The fence does not need the CI git wrapper to do that. Both sides already run the same one-PR checks once the bytes are in hand.

The empty-allow-list half does not hold. A failed policy read is a different event from a policy that was read and is level off, and from a policy file that is absent. Today those three events share one empty allow-list. That empty result is a refusal for a bound story while the merge-gate warning is off. It is an allow when that warning is on, because the write and the commit check then continue and the story layer is inactive. With two unpinned stories it also drops this story out of the contest, and the other story's allow-list can admit the write. CI already treats a failed read of this file as a refusal.

The smallest rule that keeps an unread policy from admitting a write is the fence's existing unreadable result, with the failed read named on the refusal the write hook actually returns. A missing file, and a file that reads as level off, stay on today's empty allow-list.

Question 1. The per-call limit is enough for the successful read. The CI wrapper also applies a timeout that throws, and the session git helper drops the error and the signal this fence still has to see.

Question 2. Empty allow-list plus a sentence on the refusal leaves the allows above in place. The unreadable result is the closed shape those consumers already implement.

Question 3. The commit-time staged-blob read is the only other whole-file git capture on this hook with no limit. A failed read there does not admit the planning shortcut. The deposited pre-commit hook's git calls return names, and the file bytes come from disk. The deposited pre-push hook's branch check returns a name. Its content hash already stops at 16 MiB and fails closed.

### 1. A failed policy read is not an empty allow-list (blocks-the-design)

Evidence. `readMergeBasePolicyRaw` maps a spawn error, a signal, or any other git failure to `{ kind: "error" }` with no detail (`packages/core/src/policy/write-fence.ts` 544-552). `loadOnePrMintFence` turns that into `emptyFence()` (672-680), the same view as level off. The brief read beside it already returns an unreadable fence for the same class of git error (513-541). CI does the other thing: a failed merge-base read of this file becomes `kind: "refuse"` with the read failure in the reason (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts` 1057-1062), before `evaluateOnePrScopeProofGate`. That gate treats null and unparseable text as level off (`packages/core/src/policy/one-pr-scope-proof.ts` 190-223).

Failure mode. Empty and unreadable already diverge, and the recommended mechanism keeps the empty side.

- While `plan.policy.mergeGateContext` matches a required status check, `warn` records the refusal and returns true (`packages/core/src/hooks/merge-gate-signal.ts` 79-108, `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts` 1522-1527). The write hook then continues (`dispatcher.ts` 3143-3144). The default project runtime policy is disabled (`packages/core/src/policy/runtime-authority.ts` 67-74), so an empty story fence is inactive and the write is allowed (`write-fence.ts` 827-832, `dispatcher.ts` 1659-1663). An unreadable fence is refused before that, at `dispatcher.ts` 1649-1657.
- The same warning lets a product commit through when the scope-cover result is `advisoryCapable` (`dispatcher.ts` 5712-5720 and 5536-5538). The unreadable result has no such flag (5702-5710).
- An empty allow-list is non-fencing, so an unpinned one-PR brief is dropped when any other brief has a fence (`packages/core/src/hooks/scope.ts` 276-284 and 518-524). The remaining story's allow-list can admit the write. An unreadable brief stays in the set, and two fencing briefs are a not-ready scope.

This checkout's project definition has no `mergeGateContext` field, so the reported bound-story writes stay on the hard refusal. The allow is still the behavior of the same hook wherever that field is set, and the unpinned drop does not need the warning.

`formatPositiveGoverningAllowDeny` reads only a rejected mint (`scope.ts` 85-89). On the common path the positive-allow refusal fires before the runtime-policy refusal, so switching the view to unreadable without changing that text leaves the generic no-allow-list message. Pain P2 stays open either way until that text carries the read failure.

Disposition. M2 cannot bind as "still a refusal, same advisory flag, same partition, plus a sentence." The policy-read error has to take the existing unreadable fence, with a short reason kept from the spawn. The positive-allow text has to include `unreadableDetail` when it is set. A missing blob and a parsed level of off stay empty, so the activation window stays. That reuses a refusal the brief read and the runtime hook already have. It is the recorded constraint that an unread policy does not admit a write. The extra closure is real: scratch outside the repo skips the positive-allow check (`dispatcher.ts` 3165-3167) and is then refused because unreadable is tested first. That scratch closure is what the recorded constraint requires. A later carve-out that re-opens scratch while the policy is unread would be a separate rule.

The strongest case for keeping the empty view is that a git outage should not change partition or turn the merge-gate warning off. That case treats an unread file as a successful read of level off. The level-off window remains available once the read succeeds, or when the blob is absent. What would flip this finding is a recorded requirement that product writes proceed while this blob cannot be read.

### 2. The 64 MiB option removes the reported refusal only while the error check stays (sharpens-framing)

Evidence. `gitFenceSpawn` captures with `encoding: "utf8"` and no `maxBuffer` (`write-fence.ts` 247-261). `readMergeBasePolicyRaw` returns `kind: "error"` when `result.error` or `result.signal` is set, before it looks at status (549).
